articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan National Assembly President Jorge Rodriguez from Sanctions List
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of Jorge Jesus Rodriguez Gomez, the President of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list. This action lifts sanctions against a key figure in the Venezuelan government and brother of interim President Delcy Rodriguez.

Rodriguez Gomez had been designated in September 2018 as part of a coordinated effort against the inner circle of former President Nicolás Maduro. His delisting follows the removal of his sister, Delcy Rodriguez, from the OFAC list in April of this year, and is part of a broader normalization of relations between Washington and Caracas.

This decision is seen as a significant step in Washington's diplomatic recognition of the interim Venezuelan government and aligns with a three-phase plan for Venezuela's stabilization and political transition. Jorge Rodriguez is a central figure in the ongoing transition dialogue between the Chavista government and the opposition.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cartel del Noreste Facilitators and Horse Racing Enterprise in Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Action
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism designations, targeting individuals and entities associated with the Cartel del Noreste (CDN) in Mexico. The action specifically adds Gamaliel Garza Elias and Gamaliel Garza Garcia to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.

These individuals are linked to a horse racing enterprise and an expansive criminal network operating within the CDN. Several entities, including 'CLUB LA MOLIENDA,' 'CONSTRUCCIONES Y EDIFICACIONES GARZA ELIAS, S.A. DE C.V.,' and 'CUADRA SAN DIBANH,' were also added to the SDN list for their involvement in illicit activities.

The designations highlight the ongoing efforts by the U.S. Treasury to disrupt the financial networks of transnational criminal organizations and terrorist groups, particularly those involved in illicit drug trafficking and other destabilizing activities.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for $11.6 Million Over Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an $11,662,930 settlement with Bank of America, N.A. The settlement resolves 475 apparent violations of various OFAC sanctions programs, including those targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

The apparent violations stemmed from Bank of America processing payments involving blocked banks, failing to adequately prioritize alerts for customers matching blocked persons, not promptly updating watchlists after OFAC designations, and mishandling business accounts associated with blocked individuals due to human error.

OFAC determined that the violations were non-egregious but largely not voluntarily self-disclosed, leading to no reduction in the base penalty for remedial measures or cooperation. This settlement is part of a larger enforcement action by the U.S. Treasury, which also included significant penalties from FinCEN and the OCC.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, Designates International Criminal Court, and Removes Burma-Related Designation
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, a freight forwarding firm, for $175,015. The settlement addresses four apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and six apparent violations of the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations.

Pegasus Worldwide Logistics was found to have dealt in blocked property by facilitating the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company between September 2023 and February 2024. Additionally, the firm failed to fully respond to an OFAC subpoena for six months.

In separate actions, OFAC also designated the International Criminal Court (ICC) and issued several related General Licenses (GL 13, GL 14, GL 15, and GL 16) authorizing certain transactions involving the ICC. Concurrently, a Burma-related designation was removed from the SDN List.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New General License Authorizing Russian-Origin Diesel Fuel Transactions
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Russia-related General License (GL) 135, titled "Authorizing Transactions Related to the Sale, Delivery, Offloading, and Importation of Diesel Fuel of Russian Federation Origin." This license temporarily authorizes certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations or Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The new General License permits the sale, delivery, offloading, and importation of Russian-origin diesel fuel, including into the United States, through April 7, 2027. This move comes amidst global energy market instability and follows an announcement by the U.S. President regarding the release of Russian diesel fuel to global markets.

While the GL aims to provide potential relief for global energy markets, it faces legal uncertainty, with some lawmakers arguing it conflicts with the 2022 Russian energy import ban. The authorization specifically excludes debits to accounts of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, the National Wealth Fund, or the Ministry of Finance at U.S. financial institutions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Shipping Network, Issues New Iran-Related and Amended Russia-Related General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations targeting a shadow fleet network involved in Iranian oil shipments. Concurrently, OFAC issued Iran-related General License EE, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving Samudra Marine Services Private Limited.

In addition to the Iran-related actions, OFAC also issued an amended Russia-related General License 13S, which authorizes certain administrative transactions prohibited by Directive 4 under Executive Order 14024.

The designations include individuals such as Harishyam Hariharan Chundakattil, Ketan Manohar Kochikar, and Dhwani Nisarg Vora, all Indian nationals, and entities like SSPL Solutions Private Limited, for their roles in supporting Iranian oil sanctions evasion.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ, Removes Iraq-Related Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has published an Iran-related Alert titled "Notice to Foreign Financial Institutions Conducting Business with Iran." This alert provides crucial guidance regarding sanctions risks associated with engaging in transactions with Iran.
Alongside the new alert, OFAC also published an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 156), offering further clarification on existing sanctions policies.

In a separate action, OFAC announced several designations removals, specifically delisting numerous individuals and entities previously designated under the Iraq-related sanctions program. These removals include individuals such as Abdul Hussein Abbas, Rasem Ahmad, and Wallid Issa Ahmad.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities in Counter Terrorism Action, Citing Hamas Fundraising
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Counter Terrorism designations, adding three individuals and two France-based organizations to its Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT) list.

Treasury stated that a network linked to these designations raised over $2 million for Hamas between 2020 and 2026, with hundreds of thousands of dollars reportedly sent in cryptocurrency to a Gaza-based recipient. The designated individuals are Saleem Abdallah Saleem al-Zaq, Faouzi Barika, and Amel Oualid, while the entities are Association Baraka and Ensemble C Mieux.

These actions underscore the U.S. government's commitment to disrupting financial support networks for terrorist organizations and highlight the increasing focus on cryptocurrency in illicit finance. U.S. persons are generally required to block the property of these designated parties.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Procurement Networks and Transnational Criminal Organization, Issues Iran-Related Determination and Amended FAQ
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates, targeting individuals and entities involved in Iranian procurement networks. Concurrently, OFAC designated a transnational criminal organization (TCO) known as 'A7 Network,' operating across Russia, Kyrgyzstan, Nigeria, and Zimbabwe.

The Iran-related designations include individuals such as Mehnoosh Poursaraf Hamedani and Ramin Keshvardoust, both Iranian nationals with alternative Dominican nationality, and entities like Bonasol Group Co., Limited, Dominion Trading Group Limited, and East Concord Development Limited, all based in Hong Kong. These entities are linked to Iranian sanctions evasion activities.

Additionally, OFAC published a Determination Pursuant to Executive Order 13902 concerning the automotive and rail sectors of the Iranian economy, and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 831), providing further guidance on sanctions policies.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Transnational Criminal Organizations and Counter Terrorism Actors, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs). Among the newly designated is Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre, also known as "Prometheus" and "The Engineer," a Venezuelan national linked to the TCO Tren de Aragua.

Additionally, OFAC designated Enigma Community, S. de R.L. de C.V., a Mexico-based entity, for its role in TCO activities. These actions aim to disrupt financial networks supporting criminal and terrorist operations.

In a separate set of actions, OFAC also announced the removal of several designations related to Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya sanctions programs. These removals include entities such as PATRACA, S.A. DE C.V., and individuals like Alejandro Mejia Castillo.

articles.headline: Bank of America Fined $11,662,930 by OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to pay $11,662,930 to settle its potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations of various OFAC sanctions programs. The violations involved transactions related to Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

The apparent violations occurred due to issues such as processing payments involving blocked banks, failing to prioritize alerts for sanctioned individuals, not promptly updating watchlists, and mishandling business accounts associated with blocked persons.
OFAC determined that the violations were non-egregious but largely not voluntarily self-disclosed, resulting in no mitigation for remedial measures or cooperation in the settlement amount.

body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics has agreed to pay $175,015 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations. The freight forwarding firm was found to have dealt in blocked property.

Between September 2023 and February 2024, Pegasus facilitated the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company. Additionally, the company failed to fully respond to an OFAC subpoena for six months.
OFAC determined that Pegasus's conduct was non-egregious and not voluntarily disclosed, leading to the civil penalty.

The specific details of the violations were not immediately made public in the summary, but such penalties typically involve unauthorized transactions or dealings with sanctioned entities or individuals connected to Iran.

This penalty is part of OFAC's broader efforts to enforce sanctions against Iran, which include a presumption of denial for Iran-related specific licenses and recent designations targeting Iranian finance networks.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
